title: Production prompt replay prioritization with contextual clusters
creator: Elena Ramirez
description: Objective: build a repeatable sampling pipeline that produces per-domain calibration packs for production prompts by prioritizing replays using contextual clusters. Rationale: our current calibration sets overweight high-frequency queries and under-sample tail contexts (multi-turn state, user metadata variants, and rare route-parameter combinations). This leads to unpredictable accuracy regressions when moving to FP8/INT8 profiles. The proposed approach clusters real production prompt traces by a compact context signature (semantic embedding + route + turn-index + token-length bucket), then scores clusters for replay priority with a recency-weighted importance metric that combines traffic share, observed model-confidence drift, and feature sparsity. Deliverable: a dataset generation job that emits fixed-size per-domain packs (token and example budgets) with metadata for each exemplar (cluster_id, priority_score, signal-reason), plus an automation for daily refresh and a validation harness to run quantized inference and produce accuracy deltas versus float32 baseline.
plan: 1) Exploratory analysis (1 week): compute embeddings and context signatures on last 90 days; measure cluster size distribution and route overlap. 2) Scoring design (3 days): define score = alpha*recent_traffic + beta*conf_drift + gamma*sparsity + delta*business_weight. 3) Implementation (2 sprints): clustering pipeline (Faiss-based), priority sampler that enforces per-domain quotas, augmentation module (paraphrase synthesis for sparse clusters), and exporter to S3. 4) Validation (1 sprint): run FP8/INT8 calibrations on sample packs, collect accuracy metrics and calibrator logs, iterate. 5) Rollout (2 weeks): integrate with calibration orchestration and make packs available to runtime onboarding. Key PRs and artifacts: design doc, test harness, and the initial CI job for daily pack refresh.
acceptance_criteria:
- Automated job produces per-domain packs with consistent schema (example_id, prompt_text, cluster_id, priority_score, token_count, origin_date)
- Packs meet token budget constraints for small/medium/large tiers and are reproducible for a given seed
- Initial validation shows quantization accuracy delta <= 1.5% absolute on top-1 generation metric for high-volume domains, and documented failure modes for low-volume ones
- End-to-end pipeline has integration tests and a visible dashboard of top clusters and sample coverage
- Documentation (README + runbook) exists and PR reviewed by PM and Applied ML
metrics: Target metrics for initial roll: per-domain coverage >= 90% of routes that account for 95% of traffic; median cluster size within pack <= 50 examples; median priority_score drift detection lead-time >= 3 days; quantized vs float32 top-1 delta <= 1.5% for top 10 domains; pack generation wall-time < 4 hours for 90-day window.
risks:
- Overfitting packs to recent bursts; mitigated via noise floor and minimum historic anchor examples.
- Clusters may mix semantically different prompts if embedding encoder degrades across versions; mitigate by stable embed model version pinning.
- Synthetic paraphrases could introduce label drift; limit augmentation to classes with human review and low confidence.
- Token-budget contention between domains; implement strict quota enforcement and fallback sampling policy.
